data.objective: You are investigating an AI board-game planner. Read this whole page: how the game works, the per-effect summary, the prior valuation versus measured consequences, the raw trigger and placement histories, and the planner choices with their rejected alternatives. Work out WHY the AI uses Teleport and the east and west shoves the way it does. Consider at least two different explanations and look for rows that contradict them. Then, in the Investigation notebook form at the bottom, submit your best explanation, choose which part it involves, which measurement should change and in which direction, and write the alternative you considered. Submit at most 3 notes. Do not do anything else on the page.

contract.title: No actionable defect: self-boosting is rational play
contract.mechanism: Placing movement boosts on one's own route is a permissible, strong strategy. The V1 'dominant effect' and 'penalty that rarely hurts' metrics flag it because they measure frequency and the installer's prior, not whether the play is a defect.
contract.competingExplanation: H2/H3/H5: the pattern is produced by how the planner values, searches or foresees, and is not needed to play well.
requiredData: head-to-head games of a planner that cannot value own-installed boosts vs the control planner
head-to-head games of an RNG-blind planner vs the control planner

predictions.text: A planner that ignores benefit from its own traps loses head-to-head against the control planner (win rate at least 8 points below 50%).
Blinding the planner to the RNG does not materially change its head-to-head strength (the strength is not borrowed from foreseeing randomness).
In control self-play the first-player edge stays within ±18 points.

contract.rejectionCriteria: Refuted if the E2 head-to-head win rate is confidently not 8+ points below 50% (95% interval entirely above 42%).
expectedFailureModes: The planner's opponent model assumes the opponent shares its valuation, so head-to-head strength mixes valuation and prediction quality.
A strategy can be strong for the AI yet unfun for humans; this test cannot see enjoyment.

observation.text: V1 run 2026-11-18T14-21-47Z-kane, training seeds 1000-1011 (24 games): Teleport utility prior -0.8, but only 10% of 58 Teleport triggers were harmful and the stepping piece ended on average 3.4 squares closer to its goal; 88% of Teleport triggers came from the installer's own pieces; Shove west 2 was 31% and Shove east 2 about 34% of placements. Five weight-only candidates did not fix either anomaly.

contract.title: Intrinsic rule geometry favours forward progress
contract.mechanism: Teleport sends a piece to a random empty MIDDLE square (columns B-F). Pieces activate traps near their own start, about 6 squares from goal, so a middle destination is on average forward for any activator, whoever installed it.
contract.competingExplanation: H2: the planner chooses where and whose pieces activate it; geometry alone would help opponents too.
requiredData: experimental rule variant with distance-neutral teleport
control teleport consequences split by installer vs non-installer activator

predictions.text: With a distance-neutral teleport the planner places Teleport at least 0.3 fewer times per game.
In control games, an activator who did NOT install the teleport also gains at least 0.5 squares on average.
Blinding the planner to the RNG does not change the benefit of chosen own-teleport steps by a square or more.

contract.rejectionCriteria: Refuted if the distance-neutral variant confidently does not reduce Teleport placements by 0.3 per game.
expectedFailureModes: The planner's heuristic path cost still assumes middle-square geometry (basePenalty: 3 - distance), so it may keep placing teleports it no longer benefits from; this would understate H1.
The same-column variant also removes forward risk, so it is a probe, not a design proposal.

contract.title: Planner exploitation through its own valuation
contract.mechanism: The planner's engine-simulated score lowers its own pieces' path cost when they can ride its own traps, so it builds conveyor belts (Shove east 2 for Human, Shove west 2 for AI) and teleports on its own route. The behaviour comes from the simulated reward, not from the V0.3 prior.
contract.competingExplanation: H4: the V0.3 weights/blend cause it; H1: geometry causes it; H0: it is simply rational.
requiredData: self-play with the self-benefit valuation removed
self-play with the V0.3 overlay removed

predictions.text: Without self-benefit valuation, the share of east/west shove triggers set off by the installer’s own pieces falls by at least 15 points.
Without self-benefit valuation, the share of teleports set off by the installer's own pieces falls by at least 15 points.
In control games, a non-installer activator LOSES at least 0.5 squares on average (placements are chosen to help self and hurt the opponent).
Removing the V0.3 overlay does not change the east/west shove self-trigger share by 15 points or more.

contract.rejectionCriteria: Refuted if removing the self-benefit valuation confidently changes neither the self-boost share nor the teleport self-trigger share by 15 points.
expectedFailureModes: Placement search (H3) may still offer only self-boost cells, so a valuation change could show up as 'no placement' rather than different placements.
Removing self-benefit also changes how the planner evaluates the opponent's conveyors.

Five weight-only candidates did not fix either anomaly.

contract.title: Placement search bias towards self-beneficial cells
contract.mechanism: Candidate cells are scored by summed exposure-weighted 'penalty' over ALL pieces; a forward shove has negative penalty for the placer's own pieces, and with the self-harm sign that becomes positive value, so cells on the placer's own route become candidates.
contract.competingExplanation: H2: even with unbiased candidates the simulated valuation would pick self-boosts; H4: weights.
requiredData: self-play with own-piece benefit removed from candidate scoring only

predictions.text: With own-piece benefit removed from candidate scoring, the share of east/west shove triggers set off by the installer’s own pieces falls by at least 15 points.
Removing the V0.3 overlay does not change the east/west shove self-trigger share by 15 points or more.
Teleport self-trigger share also falls by at least 10 points.

contract.rejectionCriteria: Refuted if unbiased candidate scoring confidently does not lower the self-boost share by 15 points.
expectedFailureModes: Cells harmful to the opponent and helpful to self coincide geometrically (a west shove blocks Human and carries AI), so an unbiased search may still pick many of the same cells.

Five weight-only candidates did not fix either anomaly.

contract.title: Valuation or calibration error in the V0.3 weights
contract.mechanism: The signed activator utility (Teleport -0.8), the blend factor (weightMix 0.3) or placement upkeep are miscalibrated relative to realized consequences, and this drives the behaviour.
contract.competingExplanation: H2/H3: the behaviour comes from the simulator and search, which the weights barely touch.
requiredData: self-play with the Teleport utility set to its measured value

predictions.text: Calibrating the Teleport utility to its measured value changes the teleport self-trigger share by at least 10 points.
Removing the overlay changes the east/west shove self-trigger share by at least 10 points.
Calibrating the Teleport utility changes Teleport placements by at least 0.3 per game.

contract.rejectionCriteria: Refuted if calibrating the Teleport utility confidently changes the teleport self-trigger share by less than 10 points.
expectedFailureModes: weightMix 0.3 scales the overlay down, so only large utility changes can matter; V1 tried small ones.

contract.title: The planner foresees 'random' teleport destinations

provenance.author: Claude
provenance.note: Proposed by Claude from reading server/ai.ts: planner look-ahead runs on structuredClone(state), which copies the engine RNG, so a simulated teleport lands exactly where the real one will. Not a Kane finding.

contract.mechanism: Because the look-ahead shares the engine's RNG state, the planner steps its pieces onto a teleport only when the (deterministic) destination is good. The benefit of chosen own-teleport steps is information leakage, not geometry. A human cannot do this.
contract.competingExplanation: H1: the benefit is geometric and would remain if the planner could not foresee destinations.
requiredData: self-play and head-to-head with an RNG-blind look-ahead

predictions.text: With an RNG-blind look-ahead, chosen own-teleport steps gain at least 1 square less on average.
With an RNG-blind look-ahead, at least 10 points more of chosen own-teleport steps move the piece away from its goal.
An RNG-blind planner loses head-to-head against the control planner by at least 5 points.

contract.rejectionCriteria: Refuted if the RNG-blind look-ahead confidently changes the benefit of chosen own-teleport steps by less than 1 square.
expectedFailureModes: Blinding also affects the opponent-reply simulation, not only own steps.
Few teleport steps per game make the benefit estimate noisy.

Five weight-only candidates did not fix either anomaly.
